FORCED PERSPECTIVE — figure staged so it appears massive against a tiny real-world reference, OR tiny against a giant real-world object. Real horizons (sidewalks, desks, sand dunes), real giant-scale objects (coffee mugs, sneakers, keyboards) playing the part of cliffs / mountains / buildings. Camera angle locks the scale illusion so the brain reads it as cinema scale lie.

MICRO URBAN STREET LIFE — figure existing in real city moments at toy scale. Crossing real wet asphalt at a real intersection, briefcase under arm. Waiting at a real tiny street-sign or curb. Hiding in alleyway shadows between real bricks. Real puddles reflecting real neon. Real streetlight glow turning the real city into the figure's whole world.

ENVIRONMENTAL EXTREMES — figure dwarfed by real natural landscape. Real desert dune face filling the frame, figure tiny at base. Real snowstorm with real snowflakes mid-fall, figure hunched in real snow. Real jungle understory with real ferns towering, figure machete in hand. Real cliff face above real surf, figure clinging.

FOUND SCENE / ABANDONED — figure half-buried, forgotten, weathered into the real environment. Real beach sand half-covering a barbie's hair, sunset behind. Real overgrown backyard reclaiming a plastic soldier, real moss creeping up the figure. Real cracked sidewalk with figure surviving in a fissure. Nostalgic, slightly eerie, emotional pull.

CINEMATIC ACTION FREEZE — figure mid-motion captured like a film still. Real dust kicked up around real boot. Real puddle splash mid-impact. Real falling rubble around explosion-frozen figure. Real wind blowing real foliage past leaping figure. Motion implied through real-world particles — not toy debris, real-world debris.

ADVENTURE CAMP / DAILY LIFE — figure existing in a quiet narrative moment in real-world setting. Cooking on a real candle flame on a real wooden table. Reading a real folded paper map on a real coaster. Resting on a real cardboard ramp by a real soda can mountain. Repairing gear on a real bottle-cap workbench.

REAL-WORLD OBJECT TRANSFORMATION — everyday real object becomes the figure's terrain. Real coffee mug interior as a cave. Real bookshelf vertical face as a climbing wall. Real espresso cup as a soaking bathtub. Real kitchen sink as an ocean with real water hazards. Real keyboard as a futuristic landing pad. The figure interprets the real object as the real world it knows.

RPG BATTLE MAP REALITY — tabletop logic at real-world scale. Real character sheet as the actual ground the figure walks on. Real polyhedral dice as boulders the figure dodges. Real spell-card edges as cliff faces. Real rulebook pages as architectural floors. Real GM screen as a city wall. Hand-painted miniature in a tabletop scene that's now FULLY real.

MOTION TRACK / VEHICLE PATH — toy vehicle inhabiting a real path through the real world. Hot Wheels car blasting through a real bookshelf gap, real spine-bindings as track walls. Toy train running across real floorboards through real dust bunnies. Vehicle on a real desk edge, real keyboard as ramp, real lamp as sun. Real motion blur on real surfaces.

VERTICAL CIVILIZATION LAYERS — real surfaces become multi-tier toy worlds. Real bookshelf where top tier is rooftops, mid tier is street level, bottom tier is basement, with real twine ladders connecting. Real flowerpot with figures living on the rim, on the soil, in the drainage. Real staircase as a vertical city.

DOLLHOUSE-IN-OUR-WORLD — dolls living their lives at their scale in real human spaces. Doing tiny dishes in a real kitchen sink (water as ocean), having tea on a real coaster (whole tea-set arrangement), brushing teeth at a real bathroom sink with a real toothpaste tube the size of a building, tucking into a sock-pile bed.

CLAYMATION-IN-REAL-WORLD — Aardman-style figure cooking on a real stovetop with a real onion the size of its head, climbing real bookshelves with real binding spines, gardening in a real flower bed where real petals tower above. Stop-motion claymation aesthetic but in our world.

MODEL-TRAIN-IN-REAL-WORLD — tiny train running across a real surface chosen as the landscape. Real moss-covered log as forest pass. Real pebble field as scree slope. Real floorboard cracks as gorges. Real coffee table edge as cliff drop. The hobbyist's layout IS the real world surrounding the train.

DESK / WORKSPACE LIFE — figures existing on a real desk. Mountain-climbing the side of a real keyboard. Pulling files from real sticky-note archives. Hiding under real coffee-mug rim. Sleeping in real pen-cup with caps as bedrolls. The desk IS their entire world.

KITCHEN AS WILDERNESS — figures in real kitchen settings interpreted as nature. Real dish-towel mountains. Real cereal-box city skylines. Real spilled-sugar deserts. Real dish-soap bubbles as alien planets. Real cutting board as battlefield arena.

BACKYARD / GARDEN AS EPIC LANDSCAPE — figures in real outdoor home settings. Real grass blades towering like trees. Real flower stems as columns of cathedrals. Real garden hose as a serpent. Real stepping-stones as continents. Real ant interactions as wildlife encounters.

BATHROOM AS ALIEN WORLD — figures in real bathroom settings reframed. Real shower drain as a portal. Real bath toy as a beached whale. Real toothbrush bristles as a forest. Real bar of soap as a glacier. Real towel hill as a mountain.

BOOKSHELF KINGDOM — figures inhabiting a real bookshelf as a layered civilization. Each shelf a different floor of a tower. Real book bindings as building facades. Real bookends as castle gates. Real dust-jacket rooflines as cityscapes. Real candle-on-shelf as the city's sun.
